correctness.rationale: The exact same U_q(n) lower bound is established in Kumallagov Proposition 3.2 by applying the factor-two BWT amplification inequality to the Lyndon rotation, whose endpoints differ and thus whose linear and cyclic run numbers agree. For the upper bound an independent bounded program parsed the witness file with duplicate-key rejection and checked the exact set of 67 keys. For each row it verified length, ternary support and n-1 unequal adjacent output pairs; reconstructed a candidate by traversing Psi, the inverse of stable-ranked LF; verified n distinct length-n rotations and recovered the stated BWT by sorting them and extracting last letters; and counted exactly ceil(n/2) cyclic input changes including the closing edge. The checks are exact for every listed length. A ternary solution embeds in every ordered q-letter alphabet for q>=3 without changing the order of its rotations or any run count.
residual_risks: Exact finite certificate, not evidence of a universal proof or of a classification of all extremizers. Linear output and cyclic input runs must not be interchanged.

evidence: The broad relaxation attains ceil(n/2), but the one-cycle question remains open there.

Fici et al. construct unclustered BWTs at arbitrary lengths, using generalized de Bruijn and insertion/deletion constructions, without establishing the optimal inverse run count. Remark 23 gives a sharp length-12 example, notes the ordinary ternary de Bruijn family has ratio 3/2 rather than 2, and leaves broader ratio-2 coverage open.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The relaxation drops a necessary feasible-necklace condition; unconstrained arbitrary-length output existence lacks the optimal inverse run requirement. Neither subsumes the certified minimum in the window.

originality.rationale: The actual primary preprint establishes the identical lower bound, small values and eight sharp lengths in this window: 28,29,36,37,52,53,60,61. It does not establish sharpness at the remaining 59 lengths, starting at 14; its all-length formula is a conjecture and its all-length relaxation omits one-cycle realizability. Later distinct Resultary entries cover the exact numeric assertion on 14–64 and go beyond it there in some respects; one even has the exact same length-14 certificate. Credit that overlap without inferring independent discovery or priority. The complete finite interval, in particular its tail 65–80 beyond those later consecutive ranges, was not already established by the inspected statements.
residual_risks: There may be further finite tables, unpublished certificates or a broad theorem not located. Dates and a shared witness do not identify certificate provenance or establish independent priority. Prior overlapping exact values must not be advertised as individually new.

value.rationale: This closes the first consecutive block of unchecked lengths after the previously established small cases for a named natural extremal problem, rather than choosing isolated favorable parameters. Relative to the primary preprint it fills 59 explicit gaps; the checked neighboring records still do not cover the continuous tail 65–80. The full prefix is a compact exact testbed for potential constructive proofs and rules out any counterexample at the certified lengths. The numerical endpoint is a certificate extent, not a claimed phase transition or an extrapolation.
residual_risks: No infinite construction or exhaustive classification of minimizers; if further blanket coverage appears, the finite extension's value and originality would need reassessment.
